device.category: 6-voice analogue polyphonic desktop synthesizer with digital reverb, USB powered
device.based_on: Original design (Greece, 2021), inspired by the simplicity of the Sequential Six-Trak.

sources.title: Dreadbox Nymphes Owner's Manual V2.0
sources.note: Features, power, quick start, every slider parameter, presets, menu (modes, chords, LFO 2, reverb, mod sources, MIDI/MPE), global settings, SysEx, preset list, CC list (image, read by OCR and checked).

architecture.polyphony_mode: POLY (6 voices), UNI A (6 per note), UNI B (4 per note), TRI (3 notes x 2), DUO (2 notes x 3), MONO; chords in the unison-type modes; MPE
architecture.patch_memory_note: 49 user and 49 factory presets in banks A-G, 1-7 (each location holds both); chords, mod routings and reverb stored per preset.
architecture.summary: Per voice: an analogue oscillator whose WAVE morphs saw, square and triangle (with pulse width), a square sub an octave down, white noise, a 24 dB resonant low-pass filter (32.7 Hz-16.7 kHz, self-oscillating), a filter ADSR (also to pitch), an amp ADSR and a polyphonic LFO 1 to pitch and cutoff. The six voices pass a 6 dB high-pass and a digital reverb. LFO 2 (monophonic) and mod wheel, velocity and aftertouch reach most slider parameters. Glide, detune and chord sliders; six play modes.

modules.name: MIDI and voice assigner
modules.description: Receives MIDI over 3.5 mm TRS or USB (no keyboard); assigns six voices per play mode, plays programmed chords, glide (fixed rate, polyphonic), detune; MPE.

modules.name: Oscillator
modules.description: Analogue VCO with WAVE morphing saw > square > triangle; pulse width on the pulse part.

modules.name: Sub oscillator
modules.description: Square one octave below the oscillator.

modules.name: Low-pass filter
modules.description: 24 dB/oct resonant low-pass, 32.7 Hz-16.7 kHz, self-oscillates at maximum resonance; tracks 1:1 at full TRACK.

modules.name: Filter envelope
modules.description: ADSR to filter cutoff (EG) and oscillator pitch (oscillator EG); unipolar.

modules.name: VCA
modules.description: Voice amplitude under the amp envelope.

modules.name: LFO 1
modules.description: Polyphonic, bipolar: triangle, saw down, saw up, square, random; low, high, track or BPM rate; delay and fade (one-shot with delay 0, fade full); key sync. Fixed to pitch and cutoff.

modules.name: LFO 2
modules.description: Monophonic, bipolar, same controls as LFO 1; assignable to the first 12 sliders' 24 parameters.

modules.name: High-pass filter
modules.description: 6 dB/oct non-resonant high-pass on the summed voices (with the low-pass, a band-pass).

modules.name: Reverb
modules.description: Digital reverb: size, decay, low-pass filter, mix; the only digital stage.

modules.name: Output
modules.description: Volume to the line output and headphones.

mod_matrix.note: Each source has its own depth for every destination, set by moving the slider with the source's menu page open (slider position = depth). Mod wheel, velocity and aftertouch add to the slider value (clipping at the top); LFO 2 mixes in, so at full depth the slider value no longer matters. LFO 2 cannot modulate LFO 1 or LFO 2 parameters (24 destinations). Destination IDs are the depth CC numbers (CC 38 is unused). Reverb destinations are reachable by CC; the manual's text lists 28 slider destinations.

indicators.label: SHIFT, MENU, LOAD and SAVE LEDs
indicators.function: SHIFT state, menu and submenu (blinking speed), load and save (blink patterns), MPE state on the MIDI page.

behaviours.name: SHIFT
behaviours.rule: 14 sliders control 28 parameters: bottom labels normally, top labels while SHIFT is held or latched (double-click).

behaviours.name: Signal path
behaviours.rule: Per voice: oscillator, sub and noise mixed into the 24 dB low-pass, then the VCA. Voices summed into the 6 dB high-pass (band-pass with the low-pass) and the digital reverb.

behaviours.name: Fixed modulation
behaviours.rule: LFO 1 (polyphonic) only reaches pitch and cutoff; the filter envelope only reaches cutoff and pitch (unipolar). One-shot LFO: DELAY 0 and FADE full.

behaviours.name: Assignable modulation
behaviours.rule: Open MENU 2, 4, 5 or 6 and move sliders: each slider position sets that source's depth on that parameter. Hold MENU 1 s on a source page to clear it. Polyphonic aftertouch and MPE reach the listed per-voice targets.

behaviours.name: Play modes and chords
behaviours.rule: POLY 6 notes; UNI A 6 voices per note; UNI B 4; TRI 3 notes x 2 voices; DUO 2 notes x 3; MONO 1. In UNI A, UNI B, TRI and DUO the CHORD slider picks one of seven chords programmed by playing them; CHORD can be modulated.

behaviours.name: Presets
behaviours.rule: LOAD, choose bank (SHIFT on) and preset (SHIFT off), then click for the user preset or hold for the factory preset. SHIFT + SAVE, choose, SAVE. Loading sends the preset as SysEx; a full dump sends user then factory presets.

behaviours.name: Tuning and power
behaviours.rule: Warm up 5-10 minutes, then auto-tune with MENU + LOAD (about a minute, audible). Use a good 1 A USB supply on the same mains as the audio gear; poor supplies cause noise, wobbly oscillators or no boot.

source_inconsistencies: Key features say 'MIDI in/out over USB or via MIDI out via DIN5', but the panel has a 3.5 mm MIDI IN and the supplied cable is a DIN-to-3.5 mm input adapter.
The filter text says the high-pass follows the low-pass in series per voice; the block diagram places it after the six voices are summed.
Section 5.9 says each of mod wheel, velocity and aftertouch reaches 28 slider destinations; the CC list adds four reverb destinations (CC 86-89) and LFO 2 delay/fade.
The CC list has no CC 38; destination depths run 31-37 and 39-63.
The CC list labels the amp envelope depth rows 'Mod Source Filter AMP Attack Depth' etc.

modelling_gaps.detail: Voice modules are modelled once (per_voice); LFO 2, high-pass, reverb and output are common.
Each of four sources has a depth for each of 36 destinations; modelled as a dense matrix keyed by depth CC.
The menu map is an image; LFO type, key sync and legato are placed in the menu by inference.
